advisor.summary: Loss harvesting realizes the portfolio's unrealized losses against the year's recognized gains, with any net loss absorbing up to $3,000 of ordinary income and the excess carrying forward with its character intact. The mechanics are settled law; the entire discipline is operational — selling the right lots, staying invested through a non-substantially-identical replacement, and keeping every household account outside the §1091 wash-sale window. Short-term losses that absorb short-term gains save ordinary rates and are the highest-value harvest. The mirror-image move, realizing long-term gains inside the 0% bracket in low-income years, is a companion this model does not compute — the modeled inputs are harvested losses only, with netting, the $3,000 limit, and carryforward all handled by the engine. Nothing here should ever drive an investment decision the portfolio would not survive on its own merits.
mechanics: Netting runs short-against-short and long-against-long before cross-netting; a remaining net capital loss offsets up to $3,000 of ordinary income per year under §1211(b), and the unused balance carries forward indefinitely with its short- or long-term character preserved under §1212(b).

Character targeting drives the value: short-term losses that absorb short-term gains save ordinary rates, while long-term losses absorbing long-term gains save preferential rates. The model takes the two harvested amounts separately and the engine performs the netting, the $3,000 ordinary offset, and the carryforward.

§1091 disallows a loss when substantially identical securities are acquired within 30 days before or after the sale — a 61-day window that counts dividend reinvestments, a spouse's accounts, and IRA purchases; the disallowed loss ordinarily shifts into the replacement's basis, but a purchase inside an IRA destroys it permanently (Rev. Rul. 2008-5). Staying invested means swapping into a similar but not substantially identical position.

The unmodeled companion: in low-income years, long-term gains stack on ordinary income under §1(h) and are taxed at 0% up to $98,900 MFJ / $49,450 single of 2026 taxable income. §1091 applies only to losses, so gains can be sold and immediately repurchased, resetting basis to market with no wash-sale issue — run it in a separate projection.
Harvested gains raise MAGI even when taxed at 0%, so §1411 NIIT thresholds, ACA premium credits, and IRMAA lookbacks all need checking before sizing either side of the play.

authority.note: Capital losses allowed against capital gains plus up to $3,000 of ordinary income per year — the ordinary-income kicker on a net-loss year.
Indefinite carryforward of unused capital losses, retaining short/long character — why over-harvesting is banked, not wasted.
The wash-sale disallowance and its 61-day window — the operational rule the whole strategy is built around.
A repurchase inside an IRA within the window disallows the loss with no basis adjustment anywhere — the foot-fault that permanently destroys the harvest.
The LTCG rate stacking that creates the 0% bracket used by the gain-harvesting companion move.
NIIT attaches on MAGI over $200k/$250k — harvested gains count toward the threshold even when taxed at 0%.
The 2026 breakpoints — 0% bracket to $98,900 MFJ / $49,450 single taxable income — the sizing math depends on.

requirements: A taxable brokerage account — none of this applies inside IRAs or 401(k)s.
Lot-level basis records and a specific-identification election with the broker, so the intended lots are actually the ones sold.
A replacement security that is similar but not substantially identical, and 61-day-window discipline across every household account, including IRAs and a spouse's accounts.
A current-year projection showing the gains to be offset (or, for the companion move, the room under the 0% breakpoint).
risks: Wash-sale foot-faults are the leading failure mode: a dividend reinvestment, a spouse's purchase, or an IRA buy inside the 61-day window disallows the loss, and under Rev. Rul. 2008-5 the IRA variant destroys it permanently rather than deferring it.
Tracking error: the replacement position can diverge from the original during the holding window, and a harvested loss on a position about to rebound costs more than the tax it saved.
Specific-identification failures — average-cost defaults or instructions given after the trade — mean the broker's 1099-B reports different lots than the plan assumed.
Harvested gains sized past the 0% breakpoint spill into the 15% bracket and can trip AGI-driven cliffs (ACA credits, IRMAA) that cost more than the harvest saved.
stateNotes: Most states conform to the federal gain and loss computation through a federal-AGI starting point, but nearly all tax gains at ordinary state rates with no 0% bracket — the federal 0% is not a state 0%.
No PTET interaction — this is individual portfolio-level planning with no entity election involved.

Missouri is the special case: the 2025 capital-gains legislation (RSMo §143.121, HB 594) lets individuals subtract 100% of federally reported capital gains, so Missouri no longer taxes these gains at all — harvesting is a federal-only play for Missouri residents, and a harvested loss produces no additional Missouri benefit.
reviewChecklist: Lot-level unrealized gain/loss report pulled, holding periods confirmed, and the modeled short/long harvested amounts match actual harvestable lots.
Replacement securities vetted as not substantially identical, and the 61-day calendar checked across every household account including IRAs.
Specific-lot identification instructions delivered to the broker before the trades, not after.
Dividend reinvestment switched off on positions slated for harvest.
Carryforward schedule updated in the permanent file and reconciled to the 1099-B at filing.

client.teaser: Your portfolio's down positions can pay you back at tax time.
client.headline: Use market dips to cut your tax bill — without leaving the market
plainEnglish: In any account, some holdings are up and some are down. The tax law lets you use the down ones. Sell a losing position and the loss cancels out gains elsewhere. It can also erase up to $3,000 of regular income each year. Anything left over rolls forward to future years.

You do not have to sit out of the market. Right away, you buy a similar — but not identical — investment. Your money stays invested the whole time. One rule matters most: do not buy the same thing back within 30 days, in any of your accounts.
In a low-income year, the reverse move can work too. Some profits can be sold at a zero federal rate, up to a limit. We watch for both chances every year.
client.analogy: It is like clipping coupons the market prints for you. Down days print one kind. Low-income years print another. They only go to waste if you never clip them.
benefits: Market losses become real tax savings while you stay fully invested
Up to $3,000 a year can offset your regular income
Unused losses bank automatically for future years
In low-income years, some profits can be sold federal-tax-free
steps: WE scan your accounts each fall for positions worth harvesting.
WE size the trades and hand you the exact list, with the 30-day rules spelled out.
YOU (or your investment advisor) place the sales and the replacement buys.
WE report every lot at tax time and track what carries forward.
clientCommitments: Tell us about every account — the 30-day rule counts your IRA and your spouse's accounts too
Turn off automatic dividend reinvestment on positions we plan to harvest
Place the trades on the schedule we give you, not before or after

annualMaintenance: Fall harvest scan and year-end execution check across all household accounts
Carryforward reconciliation against the 1099-B at filing
deliverables: Harvest trade list with replacement candidates and the wash-sale calendar
Carryforward tracking schedule for the permanent file
